title: Atlas Payments — integration call notes
content:
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Clarke (Redwood infra), Sofia Ramos (Atlas PM), Liam Nguyen (Atlas Eng), Priya Desai (Atlas Security)

High-level summary:
- Intro call to scope payments fraud/reconciliation integration. Atlas is evaluating Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated. Primary use: real-time routing and fraud scoring for transactions, plus periodic embeddings for merchant lookup and dispute triage.
- Key constraints: PCI scope minimization, strict latency (p95 < 150ms for scoring), throughput target ~200 req/s steady with spikes to 800 req/s on black friday-like events. Audit/logging + KMS required.

Requirements / asks from Atlas:
- PCI-safe integration pattern (no raw PAN to hosted API). They want tokenization + token->context enrichment in their VPC, then send only tokenized metadata to Redwood.
- Option for Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment; must support customer-managed KMS and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM (Splunk).
- SLA: 99.95% uptime, p95 latency guarantees for scoring. Need RBAC for team access and per-route quotas.
- Data retention: transaction context kept for 90 days for evals; raw transaction storage must be opt-out.
- Traceability: request IDs surfaced to Atlas logs, ability to fetch request traces for forensic review.
- Model requirements: baseline open-model used for scoring + ability to pin model versions; regression alerts on false-positive/negative rate.
- Integration: two phases — (1) scoring endpoint + webhook results; (2) batch embeddings for merchant similarity every 24h.

Technical notes / gotchas mentioned:
- PCI: Atlas cannot send PAN or CVV to any third-party hosted service. Need clear guidance on redaction/tokenization flow. We proposed: Atlas tokenizes PAN internally, send token + non-sensitive context (merchant id, amount, time, device signals). Redwood would mark dataset as "tokenized" for auditing.
- Webhook delivery semantics: Atlas needs at-least-once with idempotency keys. Redwood's webhook retries/backoff pattern outlined; confirm max retry window and support for custom retry endpoints (they have strict firewalls).
- Throughput: Hosted API burst limits will likely throttle; recommend Dedicated with autoscale burst capacity. Also discuss connection pooling and keep-alive for lower tail latency.
- KV cache/embedding: embeddings storage needs encryption at rest with Atlas KMS. Also discuss incremental update behavior for merchant index and how long embeddings take to be available after batch job.
- Observability: Atlas wants token-level cost breakdowns per route; Redwood Console can expose token/cost but confirm mapping to Atlas internal billing keys.

Open questions (from Atlas):
- Can Redwood guarantee no full PAN/PII is logged by default? (Action: confirm logger redaction policy and provide docs)
- How long until Dedicated onboarding is complete? (Action: provide timeline & pre-reqs)
- What are the limits on webhook retry window / delivery guarantees?
- For embeddings: support for incremental updates vs full rebuilds and expected time-to-index.
- Can we surface per-request trace links to Atlas SIEM? (Action: SRE to confirm trace export options)

Next steps / action items:
- Maya: send proposed integration pattern diagram + redaction/tokenization playbook (due 2026-05-22).
- Ethan: produce Dedicated sizing proposal (GPU pool estimate, expected throughput per instance, autoscale notes) and cost ballpark (due 2026-05-25).
- Sofia: share sample (anonymized/tokenized) transaction dataset + expected peak schedule for traffic (due 2026-05-26).
- Liam: provide their webhook endpoint config & firewall constraints so we can validate connectivity (due 2026-05-24).
- Priya: security checklist inputs (compliance contacts, KMS policies) and confirm any mandatory audits (due 2026-05-27).
- Maya/Ethan: schedule technical deep-dive with Atlas eng + Redwood SRE for connection tests and trace export discussion (propose 2026-05-28).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: sending sensitive data to hosted API could expand Atlas's PCI scope. Mitigation: recommend Dedicated or Private VPC for initial rollout; provide tokenization pattern and partner with Atlas security on audit.
- Risk: latency under load. Mitigation: run load-profile test in staging with Dedicated sizing; use KV cache for repeated prefixes and per-route batching tuning.
- Risk: webhook delivery blocked by their firewall. Mitigation: support polling fallback for results and provide egress checklist for their security team.

Reference links / notes to attach to ticket:
- Confluence: Atlas Payments Scope (link above)
- JIRA-5238: "Atlas integration — Dedicated evaluation" (linked artifact)
- PR: integration-atlas/pull/47 (early adapter hooks)

Quick wins for next week:
- Share tokenization playbook + sample request/response with redaction examples (low lift, high trust).
- Provide Dedicated sizing estimate so Atlas can budget.

Notes to self (internal):
- Prep demo deck showing Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs (latency, cost, PCI scope).
- Loop in legal for data processing addendum if they pick Hosted and send any PII-like fields.
- Confirm with SRE on trace export formats (OTLP/Zipkin) and whether we can push request traces to Atlas Splunk/Hec endpoint.

Status: draft — will update after engineering deep-dive and once Atlas shares sample dataset.

-- Maya
